To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the numerical model developed in this work is a useful and powerful tool to simulate the stamping process, (2) the numerical model can be used to predict the forming limit of the structure, (3) a damage criterion is necessary to predict the forming limits of the structure.

(i) the classical stamping process is well predicted with the PamStamp2G code and the isotropic hardening law with the isotropic and mixed yield criteria and (ii) the rolling process is well predicted using the same code and the same law, but with the isotropic yield criterion.

the numerical simulation of the classical clinching process with PamStamp2G is possible and that the simulation of the roll clinching process is possible with the numerical tool developed in this work.

the experimental and numerical study of a cold forming process, namely, the clinching process, which is used in automotive industry for the assembly of metal sheets.
the experimental and numerical study of a cold forming process, the stamping, which is used in the last forming operations of automotive parts.
the study of the mechanical behaviour of aluminium alloys, with particular attention being paid to the effect of Bauschinger's effect, which is known to be very important for aluminium alloys.

the numerical prediction of the stamping process can be significantly improved by taking into account the anisotropy of the material, the Bauschinger effect, the mixed isotropic-kinematic hardening and the ductile damage.
